Hi all — adding the operational detail requested and confirming the remediation cadence we follow:

Summary (operationally authoritative):
- Scanning:
  - Monthly authenticated agent-driven scans (Nessus) across all prod hosts — schedule: first weekend of month, full credentialed scan.
  - Weekly unauthenticated network scans (Rapid7) every Monday 03:00 UTC targeting public IP ranges and edge services.
  - Nightly image scans via Trivy during build; failing pipelines for critical/high findings blocked until triage is attached.
  - Ad-hoc pen test / SIG tests run per-request and before major releases.

- CVE remediation targets (SLA commitments):
  - Critical: patch or mitigation in 7 calendar days; if mitigation is temporary, permanent remediation planned within 30 days.
  - High: remediation in 30 calendar days; tracked in our remediation backlog with priority tagging.
  - Medium: remediation in 90 calendar days.
  - Low: evaluated and scheduled in routine maintenance windows up to 180 days.

- Triage & workflow:
  - Findings automatically ingested into JIRA (VM-XXXX) with severity mapping; Security Ops (me) performs initial triage and assigns to owning engineering team.
  - Engineering owners must provide a remediation ETA within 72 hours of assignment or request an exception (documented and approved by Head of Security).
  - Escalation path: Security Ops -> Engineering Manager (72h) -> Head of Infra (7d) -> CISO (14d).

- Evidence retention & artifacts:
  - Scan raw outputs retained for 12 months in a read-only S3 vault (encrypted with customer-managed KMS when required).
  - JIRA remediation tickets, closure notes, and patch PRs are retained per our retention policy and included in evidence bundles.

Attached: monthly-auth-scans-summary-Apr-2027.pdf (redacted sample); I've also included an anonymized remediation ticket export.

If EdgePay wants the SLA language tightened for contract inclusion, we can produce an attestation signed by our Head of Security and Legal.

Regards,
